messages:
sanjay: heads up — saw a sharp uptick of Xid 79s on apne1 streaming hosts starting ~02:10 UTC. spike aligns with a bunch of small concurrent streaming sessions (>10 concurrency). attaching quick metric snapshot :eyes:
amelia: same pattern here on a couple of us-west2 hosts, weird that ECC counts are flat though. seems not a memory-bitflip/ECC event :thinking_face:
marco: can you paste the raw nvidia kernel log lines? want to see the exact error text (xid 79 sometimes comes with pcie reset hints)
sanjay: logs pulled, snippet below:
```
[2026-03-18T02:12:41Z] NVRM: Xid (79: 14): GPU exception on GPC 2: SError, returning to scheduler
[2026-03-18T02:12:41Z] NVRM: GPU 0: Graphics SM context info, ...
[2026-03-18T02:12:41Z] PCIe: Resetting link on GPU1
```
lei: that "Resetting link" line is telling. we saw similar in a05 last year where NVLink/PCIe retrains happened under high small-batch multiplexing. could be queue starvation -> hw timeout.
amelia: telemetry query I ran (quick):
```
SELECT xid_code, count(*) FROM gpu_errors WHERE region='apne1' AND ts > now()-2h GROUP BY xid_code;
-- result: Xid 79: 124, Xid 48: 3, Xid 13: 2
```
marco: low Xid13/48 counts, high 79 suggests link/timeout rather than decode bug. also tenant mix: mostly streaming embeddings + small completion requests with concurrency spikes.
ops-bot: auto-alert created: #gpu-health -> SLO-risk elevated for apne1 streaming cluster. runbook triggered: soft-drain candidate list generated.
sanjay: quick hypothesis: small-batch multiplexing causes PCIe/NVLink retrain under sustained interleaved kernels, hardware resets produce Xid79 but ECC remains clean. can reproduce with multitenant stress harness (burst concurrency + small seq len).
lei: mitigation options:
- temporarily prefer single-tenant routing for hosts with >5 Xid79s in 1h
- lower max multiplex factor for streaming model pool in apne1 from 16 -> 8
- soft-drain hosts with >10 Xid79s and schedule repro test on them
- collect hw counters for PCIe link retrain frequency (pcie_link_retrain counter)

marco: propose rollout: 1) throttle multiplex factor for apne1 streaming pool now, 2) mark top 6 offending hosts soft-drain and run repro, 3) collect nvlink/pcie counters + attach to ticket

amelia: i'm on (1) now — changing pool config: `max_multiplex=8` for streaming-apne1 and reloading router. will monitor for 10m then escalate.
sanjay: dropping a quick repro command for infra tests (run on repro cluster):
```
./stress_streamer --model embed-1024 --concurrency 12 --batch-size 1 --duration 300 --trace-errors > /tmp/repro.log
grep "Xid (79" /tmp/repro.log | wc -l
```
lei: add to repro: pin to same host and enable `--nvprof` to dump link events. also capture dmesg after repro.
ops-bot: note: soft-drain list: host-az3-gpu-07, host-az3-gpu-11, host-az2-gpu-02, host-az2-gpu-04 (ids from telemetry). ticket #INF-2147 created.
marco: if repro reproduces consistently, plan is replace card under warranty for any host with persistent link retrain + Xid79 > 30 in 24h, otherwise reimage driver stack and monitor 72h.
amelia: update: after lowering multiplex, Xid79 rate dropped ~60% in first 8m. still seeing isolated single Xid events. reverting routing back will be gradual. :thumbsup:
sanjay: next steps assigned:
- amelia: finish rollback window and watch (30m)
- lei: run repro suite on soft-drain hosts and collect nvlink/pcie counters + dmesg (ticket INF-2147)
- marco: prepare warranty replacement checklist and vendor contact if hardware repros
- sanjay: update runbook with multiplex throttle as a mitigation knob and add pcie_link_retrain to alerting

marco: note for on-call: do not immediate hard-drain unless >50% of host GPU errors are Xid79 and repro confirms link retrain. soft-drain + repro first.
lei: logging tip: when grabbing kernel logs, include `sudo journalctl -k -u nvidia-drm --since "10 minutes ago"` and `sudo cat /sys/class/pci_bus/.../error` to capture link errors.
sanjay: great work team — leaving this open while we collect repro results. will update ticket and close thread once hosts cleared or RMA decided. :white_check_mark:
